uncited: **Ambiguous Face (AF):** A cell face with four same-sign ended diagonals and four $(+/-)$ edges.
An AF is separated with respect to a specific sign if the contour on the face is a rectangular hyperbola.
**DeVella's Necklace Test:** Used to distinguish topological sub-configurations (specifically for tunnels) by checking if two vertices on a diagonal are internally connected.
Based on the category and specific topological sub-configuration, select diagonals to intersect.
- If a $(+)$ cell has a $(+)$ ambiguous face: Single isosurface component occurs.
- If ambiguous faces have different signs: Single component occurs (Cases 10.2, 12.2).
- Case 7.1 (three $(+)$ AF): Three disjoint surfaces.
- Case 7.2 (two $(+)$ AF, one $(-)$ AF): Two disjoint surfaces.
- Case 7.3 (one $(+)$ AF, two $(-)$ AF): One surface.
- Case 13.1 (six $(+)$ AF): Four disjoint surfaces.
- Case 13.2 (five $(+)$ AF, one $(-)$ AF): Three disjoint surfaces.
- Case 13.3 (four $(+)$ AF, two $(-)$ AF): Two disjoint surfaces.
Find the $(+)$ vertex common to all three $(+)$ ambiguous faces.
- Case 13.4 (equal $(+)$ and $(-)$ AF, common vertex signs differ from faces): One isosurface piece.
- If 13.5.2: Use the diagonal through the common vertex of the three same-signed ambiguous faces as a ray.
Use the remaining three diagonals as rays to find points for the tunnel.
For each selected diagonal, solve the trilinear equation $f(t) = I$ along the diagonal to find the intersection point.
The trilinear function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined by the vertex values.
Return the set of computed intersection points.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per voxel, as it involves a fixed number of case checks and cubic root solving.
However, solving the cubic equation is more expensive than linear interpolation used in standard MC.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ per voxel, storing only the vertex values and selected diagonals.
Handles ambiguous configurations correctly without lookup tables.
- **When to use:** When topological accuracy is critical and the scalar field is well-approximated by trilinear interpolation.
- **When not to use:** When performance is paramount and linear approximation is sufficient.
Originated from the need to accurately extract topologies of analytical isosurfaces defined by trilinear functions.
